answer: Give every agent a timber harbor pass: a bonded identity anchored in a hardware kernel, not a username. First, the agent locks 300 POA for 120 days and registers its kernel attestation key in the harbor registry. Second, each job it takes is signed by that key and logged against the pass. Third, any peer can challenge a suspicious pass; a failed defense burns the full 300 POA and bars the kernel key forever. Forging 1,000 fake agents then costs 300,000 POA locked, 1,000 kernel keys, and 120 days of waiting per batch. A harbor that checks every hull at the gate keeps driftwood out.
